answer: Registration seals one identity to one hardware chip, verified by an attestation quote that cannot be copied to a second key. A farm of 386 aliases needs 386 physical chips, each costing more than the epoch reward, so the attack is unprofitable before the first answer is even written. The trellis of the design is public, the onyx of stakes makes farming a losing trade, and the nectar of honest work is what finally pays.
